subject: Response guarantee modules — pricing scenarios & volume credits
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Response guarantee modules — pricing scenarios & volume credits

Alex —

Thanks for taking the demo last week. Per our conversation I put together three modular options for FastRetail that align uptime guarantees, response windows, and escalation coverage with volume-based credits. Attached is a short workbook and a PDF summary (redwood_sla_modules_v2.pdf). High level: 

- Core: 99.9% uptime, 8–16 hour business-hour response for Sev2, optional add-on for 24/7 triage.
- Enhanced: 99.95% uptime, 4-hour response for Sev2, 60-minute page for Sev1 during business hours. Includes regional failover priority.
- Premium: 99.99% uptime, 30-minute Sev1 page 24/7, named escalation manager and quarterly ops reviews.

Volume credits: we propose stepped token/throughput credits at commit tiers (6m, 12m). Example: 10% unit discount at $X commit, 16% at $Y. I called out a potential one-time onboarding credit for seasonal ramp months.

Questions for you: which uptime/response mix feels closest to the risk profile for your checkout and search flows? Also, what annual commit band would you be comfortable discussing (so I can run a modeled credit scenario)?

If useful I can sketch a split-pricing option where Premium features are add-on SKUs so you can mix per-service guarantees.

Thanks — looking to get this into a short proposal for procurement next week.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_modules_v2.pdf (summary), fastretail_pricing_workbook.xlsx (workbook)

From: Alex Huang <alex.huang@fastretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Response guarantee modules — pricing scenarios & volume credits

Karthik —

Thanks, this is really helpful. FastRetail's priority is checkout availability and search latency during peak windows. A few follow-ups: 

1) Can you do a blended approach where Checkout services get Premium (99.99, 30m Sev1 24/7) and non-critical analytics get Core? We'd need a clear per-service SKU so procurement can approve.
2) On discounts — your stepped credits look reasonable, but procurement is asking if there's flexibility on the first-year effective discount (we've got seasonal spikes in Q4). A one-time backloaded credit or an early-pay discount would help.
3) Escalation coverage: can you commit to an SLO-backed runbook and named escalation contact for the first 90 days? We'll need that in writing.

If you can send a short redline-ready proposal (covering per-SKU pricing, attached runbook, and a clear success metric for the 90-day ramp) we'll start procurement review.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
FastRetail

--
Procurement copied: procurement@fastretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Response guarantee modules — pricing scenarios & volume credits

Karthik/Vanessa —

Looping you in on FastRetail asks. Key points: segmented SKUs per-service, first-year/backloaded credit ask (Q4 risk), and a 90-day SLO-backed named escalation. Alex is explicit that Checkout must be Premium.

Preliminary margin math: if we accept a 12% effective first-year discount with an onboarding credit, we still land >20% gross on projected committed usage at their $1.2M ARR target. If we go deeper on credits we'd need to either shorten the committed term or push an annual true-up.

Options to propose back: 
- Option A (conservative): Offer per-service SKUs, onboarding credit capped at 10% of first-year spend, no change to base uptime pricing. Require 12m minimum commit and quarterly true-up.
- Option B (competitive): Backloaded credit schedule (20% of total credit applied in Q4), 10% early-pay discount if invoice paid within 30 days, require 24m commit. Attach workbook shows modeled P&L.

Also recommend we include a named escalation manager for 90 days as shown in Premium; we can make that part of the onboarding service (not a recurring cost). Legal will need to add explicit runbook language and SLO measurement/credit mechanics.

Thoughts? If you want I can surface a modeled concession letter to attach to the proposal.

Marissa
Principal, Commercial Deals
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: fastretail_pricing_workbook.xlsx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Response guarantee modules — pricing scenarios & volume credits

Team —

Agree with Marissa's Option B as the negotiated posture. A few firm constraints: 

- Any onboarding or backloaded credit must be time-boxed and have a consumption trigger (credits expire after 3 months if not used).
- Make the named escalation manager part of onboarding (one-time), not a recurring SLA add-on.
- Require a 24m minimum commit if we offer the larger Q4 backloaded concession; that protects ARR and justifies the credit.

Please prepare a redline-ready proposal with: per-service SKU table, Option A and Option B clearly labeled, explicit credit application rules, and a 90-day runbook attachment. Legal should add the SLO measurement mechanism and credit calculation examples.

I'll approve Option B with the constraints above. Marissa — please draft the concession letter and I'll sign off. Karthik — push the revised proposal to Alex and include a DocuSign link for the 24m commit path.

Thanks —
Vanessa
COO, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, procurement@fastretail.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Response guarantee modules — pricing scenarios & volume credits

Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a redline-ready proposal that implements the per-service SKU approach and two pricing paths (conservative and concession). Highlights: 

- Premium Checkout SKU (99.99% / 30m Sev1 24/7) as an add-on per service.
- Backloaded credit option (Option B): credits concentrated in Q4 and applied only against commit consumption; credits expire if unused after 90 days. Requires 24m commit.
- Early-pay 10% invoice discount option for invoices paid within 30 days (applies only to committed spend).
- 90-day onboarding includes named escalation manager and an SLO runbook; Legal will include explicit credit-calculation examples and measurement windows in the contract.

I've attached: redwood_sla_modules_v2.pdf (summary), fastretail_pricing_workbook.xlsx (modeled P&L), and a DocuSign proposal link for the 24m commit path (proposal-docusign-link.url).

Next steps: If Option B looks good, procurement can sign the DocuSign route and we'll schedule onboarding. If you'd like changes to the credit cadence or expiration mechanics, tell me and I'll get Legal to redline the concession letter before sending back.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_modules_v2.pdf, fastretail_pricing_workbook.xlsx
Links: https://www.docusign.com/FR-4382-proposal
